constraints.meaning: At least one number, at most 100.
constraints.impact: Brute force, O(n·|k|), is at most about 10⁴ additions, so it is fast enough. The sliding window does it in O(n), and it is the idea the problem trains.

constraints.meaning: Every number is positive and small.
constraints.impact: A window sum is at most 99 · 100 = 9,900, so int is enough. No overflow.

constraints.meaning: The window has |k| numbers, at most n − 1. k > 0 looks forward, k < 0 looks back, k = 0 means all zeros.
constraints.impact: The window never contains code[i] itself and never goes all the way round. Handle k = 0 first: then there is no window.

bruteForce.summary: for every i, add up the |k| numbers after it (or before it) from scratch, with indices taken modulo n. O(n·|k|) time.
